newsitem.title: ITALY: Alitalia chief wants broad employee role.
newsitem.headline: Alitalia chief wants broad employee role.

text.p: Domenico Cempella, managing director of loss-making Italian state airline Alitalia, called for legislative measures to facilitate the creation of a broad-based worker shareholding in the company.
"Italian regulations clearly lack specific norms to back such initiatives," he told an informal hearing of parliament's lower house labour commission.
In June, Alitalia made a historic deal with unions on a vital rescue plan to restructure the ailing carrier.
Under the deal, Alitalia said between 20-30 percent of the group's shares would be reserved for employees after the company's recapitalisation and its eventually full privatisation.
Some 310 billion lire of a planned total three trillion lire capital increase was to be reserved for employees.

The deal for employees still held but Cempella complained about the lack of tax breaks to encourage workers taking up shares in their company and the "existing restrictions on being able to manage employee holdings of such stakes."
Referring to the rescue plan, he said it had been presented to the European Union Commission at the beginning of August.
"At the moment, it is not clear when we can expect a Commission ruling," Cempella said, adding that Alitalia Chairman Fausto Cereti was in Brussels today.
